question: Can Spot2 build a canonical point-in-time ABT layer that treats structural missingness, mutable state, semantic inconsistencies and stage-specific information correctly before the next modeling iteration?
hypothesis: A variable-aware T0/T1/T2 ABT contract will remove known leakage/semantic risks and expose better engineered representations without using future information.
primary_change: replace generic preprocessing with a canonical point-in-time feature engineering and ABT layer
secondary_changes: point-in-time spot and broker historical profiles
explicit variable treatment manifest for all 86 source columns

scoring_time.timestamp_definition: T0=leads.created_at; T1=first inquiry_at; T2=second and later inquiry_at before a scheduled_visit has already occurred

population.eligibility: Rows with a complete 30-day future observation window; dynamic rows only before an already-realized scheduled visit.
exclusions: dynamic rows after a realized scheduled visit

removed: generic global treatment of structural NaN

validation.split_description: All T0/T1/T2 rows for a lead remain in the same split. This experiment prepares data only; model benchmarking is a subsequent experiment.

items.evidence: Excluded from all stage feature contracts.
Raw fields excluded; age/inquiries/availability are reconstructed point-in-time when possible.
Current response fields are not in feature contracts.

items.source: prior inquiries plus realized prior responses
items.information_available_at: strictly before current inquiry or response_event_at <= score_time
items.evidence: add_supply_history_features applies as-of logic per current inquiry timestamp.
merge_asof(direction=backward) plus assertion that no future snapshot is used.
